original_question: For each positive integer k, determine the form of the layered permutation pattern of length k that is avoided by the largest number of permutations, equivalently the layered pattern of length k that is most easily avoided.
target_in_paper: Section 4, Are layered patterns the most easily avoided?, specifically the unnumbered open problem stated in the introduction as the fact that it is still unclear what form the most avoided layered pattern of length k has, and restated in Section 4 as the absence of any general conjecture identifying which layered patterns have the most avoiders. This is narrower than the neighboring weaker conjecture, cited from [23, Conjecture 1], that some layered pattern attains the largest Stanley–Wilf limit among all length-k patterns. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))
correct_elements: The draft correctly fixes the length k, restricts attention to layered patterns, and asks for the one that is most easily avoided, which matches the paper’s Section 4 focus and the introduction’s statement that the shape of the most avoided layered pattern of length k is unknown. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))
missing_details: It should specify that the paper is discussing classical permutation-pattern avoidance here, not vincular, bivincular, or mesh patterns. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))

It should define a layered pattern: a permutation that is a concatenation of decreasing blocks, equivalently a direct sum of decreasing permutations; the paper also notes the reverse/complement Wilf-equivalent up-layered versions. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))

The comparison should be eventual rather than pointwise in n, because the paper discusses switching phenomena in avoidance counts; the intended meaning is comparison for all sufficiently large n. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))

The counted quantity should be named explicitly as Av_λ(n), the number of permutations in S_n that avoid λ. The surrounding discussion in the paper uses avoider counts and Stanley–Wilf asymptotics. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))

The refined question should allow for ties, or at least state that identification is up to trivial Wilf-equivalent symmetries such as reverse/complement. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))

The phrase for all sufficiently large n should be made precise as: there exists N such that the stated inequality holds for every n > N; the paper explicitly formulates such eventual-order comparisons in its discussion of switching. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))

Ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, and nilpotency conditions are not applicable here; the missing data are combinatorial definitions and quantifiers, not algebraic hypotheses. ([cambridge.org](https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/surveys-in-combinatorics-2013/some-open-problems-on-permutation-patterns/1AB2350B9D1AC1C61B87978166B8E8A6))
refined_question: Fix k ≥ 1. Let L_k be the set of layered classical permutation patterns of length k, where a layered pattern is a direct sum of decreasing permutations. For λ ∈ L_k, let Av_λ(n) = |{π ∈ S_n : π avoids λ}|. Determine, up to reverse/complement Wilf-equivalent symmetries if desired, which pattern(s) λ ∈ L_k have the property that there exists N such that for every n > N and every μ ∈ L_k, Av_λ(n) ≥ Av_μ(n). In other words, determine the eventual most easily avoided layered pattern(s) of each length k. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))
justification: I did not replace your draft with the weaker neighboring conjecture mentioned in Section 4—namely, that among all patterns of length k, some layered pattern attains the largest Stanley–Wilf limit—because your draft asks for the form of the maximizing layered pattern itself. The paper explicitly separates these two issues: first, whether the overall maximizer is layered at all, and second, which layered pattern has the most avoiders. It then says there is no general conjecture for the latter, while recording Burstein/Kézdy–Snevily conjectural shapes for certain congruence classes of k mod 4 and warning that comparisons can switch as n varies. That is why the refined question keeps your scope but makes the classical setting, layeredness, and the eventual-in-n quantifier explicit. I leave the alternate formulation null because the paper does not prove an equivalence between eventual maximization of avoider counts and maximization of the Stanley–Wilf limit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))
